reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, a person is standing to the left of a three-dimensional solid made of 5 small identical cubes. The person is shown in side profile facing right toward the solid, with a horizontal dotted line extending from the person's eyes to the top-left cube of the solid. The solid is drawn in isometric projection and consists of:
- A central vertical column of 3 cubes.
- One cube attached to the back-right of the top cube of the column, at the same height as the top cube.
- One cube attached to the front-right of the middle cube of the column, extending forward toward the viewer at the middle height level.

The response options each show a flat 2D shape composed of connected unit squares:
- Option A: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square.
- Option B: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
- Option C: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square and 1 square attached to the right of the top square.
- Option D: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the top square and 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A half-turn about point P in the plane is applied to the shaded figure.

[Image: Shaded figure on dashed axes]

Which of the following shows the results of the half-turn?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with rightmost vertex at point P]

reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem diagram, a horizontal dashed line and a vertical dashed line intersect perpendicularly at point P, which is marked with a black dot and labeled P below the horizontal line. A shaded right triangle lies above the horizontal dashed line. Its bottom horizontal base lies along the horizontal dashed line, extending both to the left and to the right of point P, with the segment to the left of P being longer than the segment to the right of P. The right edge of the triangle is vertical, extending upward from the horizontal line. The hypotenuse connects the top-right vertex to the leftmost vertex on the horizontal dashed line. The vertical dashed line passes through the shaded triangle.

Option A shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the right.
Option B shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the left of P), its vertical side on the right extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the left.
Option C shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line, vertical side on the right extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the left.
Option D shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the right.
Option E shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line located entirely to the left of point P, touching point P at its rightmost acute vertex, with its vertical side on the left extending downward.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:

- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.

- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A graph of car production with time on the x-axis and total number of cars produced on the y-axis. Time goes from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. in one hour increments. Total number of cars produced goes from 0 to 400 in intervals of 50. A straight dotted line is drawn on the graph, going from the origin at 0 cars at 8 a.m., to the top right of the graph, at 4:00p.m. and 400 cars. A solid line is shown starting at the origin and going above the dotted line after 8:00a.m. and before 11:30 a.m. The solid line then goes below the dotted line from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. It again goes above the dotted line from 1:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. and ends at 400 cars at 4:00 p.m.]

The solid line (——) on the graph shows car production by the NU Car Motor Company during a particular day.

The dotted line (-----) shows what the total number of cars produced would be if the rate of production were constant.

B. What was the average number of cars produced per hour on this day?

Answer: ____

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D]

Continue to identify the tiles as shown above. On the grid below, write the letters A, B, C, or D to make a symmetrical pattern where PQ and RS would be lines of symmetry. Arrange the tiles to make a pattern.

[Image: A 4 by 4 grid with axes PQ and RS]

descriptors: All cells are correct with symmetrical geometric pattern about both axes, PQ and RS (letters or drawings).
With respect to at least one of the original tiles the other three tiles are correct.
Letters placed symmetrically with respect to both PQ and RS.
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task).

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D are shown in a row. Each tile is divided conceptually into four smaller quadrants:
- Tile A: A shaded black triangle in the upper-left corner (formed by the diagonal connecting the midpoint of the top edge and the midpoint of the left edge) and a solid black square in the lower-right quadrant.
- Tile B: A shaded black triangle in the upper-right corner and a solid black square in the lower-left quadrant.
- Tile C: A solid black square in the upper-left quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-right corner.
- Tile D: A solid black square in the upper-right quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-left corner.

Below is a 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line PQ and a horizontal line RS. P is at the top of the vertical line, Q is at the bottom; R is at the left of the horizontal line, S is at the right. Four squares are already labeled:
- Row 1 (top), column 1 (left): 'D'
- Row 2, column 4 (right): 'C'
- Row 3, column 2: 'B'
- Row 4 (bottom), column 3: 'A'
The remaining 12 squares are blank.

reference_items.figure_description:
An isometric drawing of a three-dimensional solid composed of 4 identical unit cubes:
- In the upper horizontal layer, 3 cubes form an L-shape consisting of a corner cube at the back, one cube extending forward and to the left, and one cube extending forward and to the right.
- In the lower layer, a fourth cube is situated directly underneath the forward-left cube, creating a vertical column of 2 cubes on the left side of the object. The spaces directly beneath the back corner cube and the forward-right cube are empty.

The response options show four similar objects made of 4 cubes, drawn in the same isometric perspective:
- Option A: Three cubes form an L-shape in an upper layer (a corner cube at the back, one cube extending forward-left, and one extending forward-right). A fourth cube is in a lower layer, positioned stepped down in front of the forward-left cube.
- Option B: A vertical column of 2 cubes is located on the right side (front-right). In the upper layer, extending back and to the left from the top cube of this column is a cube, and extending back and to the right from that cube is a third cube, forming an L-shape of 3 cubes in the upper layer with the 2-cube column at one end.
- Option C: Three cubes form a shape in an upper layer stepping up from a single cube in a lower layer at the front-left.
- Option D: A vertical column of 2 cubes is located on the right side (front-right). In the upper layer, two cubes extend to the left.

reference_items.figure_description:
A 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line AB (with A at the top, B at the bottom) and a horizontal line CD (with C at the left, D at the right).
Two quadrants are shaded with tile patterns:
- Top-right 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 1-2, columns 3-4):

  - Row 1, column 4: small black square in the top-right corner.
  - Row 2, column 3: small black square in the bottom-left corner.
  - Row 2, column 4: small black square in the bottom-right corner.

  - Shaded with the exact same pattern: four small black corner squares at the outer corners of the 2-by-2 quadrant, and a large black diamond centered where the four squares meet.
The top-left 2-by-2 quadrant and bottom-right 2-by-2 quadrant are entirely blank (unshaded).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
